title: governance: one tier verdict in the lib, four wordings stay in the channels
description:
Arch-gate sprint 45, candidate C1 (Worth exploring).

The governance ladder is a format law spelled four times in three wordings: `>= hard -> >= warn -> >= max` (the order and the comparison are fixed) appears at commands/status.rs:188-193 (embedded inside a write! chain, so it cannot be lifted by grep-and-move without reading), commands/doctor.rs:814-826, commands/prime/format.rs:280-295 (manifest_status_suffix) and commands/prime/format.rs:471-478 (the JSON "over_hard_limit"/"over_warn_threshold"/"approaching_limit"/"ok" field). config.rs owns Governance and effective_governance() but has no tier method. Flip a >= or reorder the ladder and four sites must move in lockstep with no compile error to catch a missed one.

Deepening: a tier verdict next to effective_governance() — count -> Tier{Hard,Warn,Approaching,Ok} plus which threshold fired. The four WORDINGS stay exactly where they are: they are channel vocabulary, pinned by the parity batteries. This is the same move as C3 (law in the lib, wording in the channel) and the cheapest place to establish the pattern.

Wins: the ladder exists once; a lib unit test that does not exist today; the four renderings stay honest because the strings are still asserted. Deletion test: deleting the tier method forces re-deriving the order at four sites — complexity concentrates.

No ADR conflict. Unassigned by default.

title: Store writer lock: flock on .mulch/.lock around load->mutate->save — parallel mulch processes silently lose records
description:
CONTEXT (2026-10-15, user request: port the seeds-0d7b writer lock to mulch):

- mulch (sprint-28 tree) does read-modify-write over .mulch/expertise/<domain>.jsonl (+ mulch.config.yaml for domain registration/auto-create) with NO inter-process exclusion: two mulch processes (two agents recording, record racing doctor --fix) both load, both rewrite_domain, the last rename wins and the other's records are silently lost (lost update). Same class as the fabro-4cfc tracker incident.
- The REFERENCE ml 0.10.7 has its own lock: utils/lock.ts withFileLock — PER-FILE O_CREAT|O_EXCL lockfile at `<file>.lock`, 50ms retry, 5s timeout (error: "Timed out waiting for lock on <path>. If no other mulch process is running, delete the lock file manually."), 30s mtime-staleness recovery, held around the whole read->dedupe->upsert->write cycle (record.ts:388ff); dry-run reads run lock-free; hooks fire outside the lock. move.ts even nests target+source locks (deadlock-prone ordering).
- Weakness of the reference form (why we deviate): a crashed holder leaves the lockfile — writers wedge up to 30s or until manual deletion; the staleness-steal can in principle double-admit a >30s holder. seeds (denkhaus/seeds, seeds-0d7b, shipped in seeds 0.8.0) solved exactly this store-wide with flock: advisory exclusive lock on .seeds/.lock via std::fs::File::try_lock, kernel-owned (released on process death — no stale-lockfile machinery), 5s acquire timeout, 25ms poll, Error::LockTimeout, Store::open_exclusive acquires BEFORE the first read and holds until drop. Proven code: crates/seeds/src/lock.rs + tests/writer_lock.rs (8 parallel creates keep every record; holder death proceeds immediately; reads never create the lock file).

DEMAND:
1. Port the seeds WriterLock as a LIB module (mulch::lock): advisory exclusive flock on `.mulch/.lock` (create + !truncate, permanent zero-byte sibling), acquired BEFORE the store's first read, held until the StoreFiles drops — the whole load->mutate->save cycle of a mutating command is atomic against other mulch processes. Store-wide granularity deliberately: one lock covers domain file + config mutations as one transaction (the reference's per-file lock leaves the domain auto-create config race open) and sidesteps move's nested-lock ordering.
2. Mutating commands open exclusive: record (incl. batch/stdin; --dry-run stays lock-free like the reference), edit, outcome, add, delete, delete-domain, move, doctor --fix (report mode stays lock-free), init (uniform). Reads (status, validate, render surfaces) stay lock-free and never create .mulch/.lock.
3. Bounded wait: 5s (25ms poll), then fail fast — plain error naming the lock path + json failure envelope, exit 1 (wording is a DEVIATION, see 4).
4. README DEVIATIONS bullet: kernel-owned flock on store-wide .mulch/.lock instead of the reference's per-file O_EXCL lockfiles with 30s staleness recovery; different timeout error; cross-domain writers serialize. Rationale: crash-safety — a dead writer cannot wedge the store, no stale-lockfile machinery (the seeds-0d7b lesson).
5. .mulch/.lock hygiene: init writes `.mulch/.gitignore` (`*.lock`) via write_missing (deviation: reference init writes no such file); existing stores add the ignore once by hand (this repo does it in this sprint). Verify the deviation is INVISIBLE to the reference: run the reference ml validate/doctor/status on a store with .mulch/.lock + .mulch/.gitignore present and pin byte-identical output vs a clean store.
6. Fabro note: the lock lives in the LIB seam (StoreFiles exclusive open), so fabro's embedded mutations get the same protection.

ACCEPTANCE:
- tests/writer_lock.rs (CLI level, port from seeds): 8 parallel `mulch record` on one fresh store -> all 8 records present, ids unique, no lost update; while a helper process holds the lock, a second record fails fast within the timeout and succeeds after release; a SIGKILLed holder -> next mutating command proceeds immediately; read commands never create .mulch/.lock while record does.
- lib unit tests in lock.rs: timeout, drop-release, waiter-handoff (port seeds' three).
- Battery stays byte-identical for single-process runs (no lock residue in twin stores); init battery gains the .gitignore deviation pin; doctor orphan/file-anchors surfaces must not flag .mulch/.lock or the .gitignore.
- Gates: nextest (workspace) + fmt + clippy -D warnings + just qualitygate green.
closeReason: Closed by sprint 29 (iterate lane, commits e6a82ae + fold c0fea0e). The store writer lock: lib lock.rs (WriterLock — advisory exclusive flock on the permanent zero-byte .mulch/.lock via std::fs::File::try_lock, 5s budget/25ms poll, kernel-owned, ported from seeds-0d7b), Error::Lock/LockTimeout, StoreFiles::locate_exclusive acquires BEFORE the config read and holds until drop (fabro embeds inherit the protection; embedders mutating a store must open exclusively — StoreFiles doc states it), open_store_mut + locate_record(exclusive) seams, every mutating command exclusive (record/edit/outcome/add/delete/delete-domain/move real runs, doctor --fix, init), dry-run + report modes lock-free exactly like the reference (incl. the reference's dry-run domain auto-create — spec-probed). DEVIATIONS bullet (README): flock vs the reference's per-file O_EXCL lockfiles w/ 30s staleness (crashed holders wedge writers there; kernel owns ours), different timeout wording, store-wide granularity covers the config auto-create race. init writes .mulch/.gitignore (*.lock) — init-battery deviation pin; this repo's own ignore added. Reference-invisibility twin-probed (ml status/validate/doctor byte-identical with .lock+.gitignore present; --fix leaves them). Tests: tests/writer_lock.rs (8 parallel records keep every record — unique dedup keys required, reads/dry-run never create the lock, holder-death immediate release, fail-fast plain+json arm) + 3 lib unit pins. Reviews: spec PASS-with-minors (3 nits: dry-run carve-out folded into README, stray .lock on NoConfig stores accepted as permanent-by-design, json pin folded), standards PASS-with-findings (should-fix private_intra_doc_links folded; acquire_with_timeout privatised; guard comment folded; bool-pair + 4x dry-run branch + time-window tests left with reasons). Out-of-scope seed filed: mulch-b911 (jsval doc link). Gates: 194/194 workspace, fmt, clippy -D warnings, qualitygate green.

title: compact: --auto silently skips unknown-type groups (reference mergeRecords throws)
description:
Found while moving the merge law into the lib (mulch-a2c9, sprint 45): an UNTESTED parity divergence in compact --auto for unknown record types.

How each side behaves with `--allow-unknown-types` (the reference applies it early and globally, cli.ts:92-94, so readExpertiseFile stays lenient) and a domain holding >= 2 records of an UNREGISTERED type that form a candidate group (stale member or >= min-group-size):

- Reference: findCandidates groups unknown types like any other (groupingKeyFor falls back to record.type, compact.ts:57-64), the auto path reaches mergeRecords (compact.ts:605), which throws `Unknown record type: ${first.type}` (compact.ts:618-620) - the command fails with that error.
- Port: find_candidates groups them the same way (commands/compact.rs find_candidates, the `_ => record_type.clone()` arm), but the auto loop does `let Some(row) = store.registry().row(&candidate.r#type) else { continue; }` at the mechanical-merge call site - the group is SKIPPED silently: no warning, no error, exit 0.

The 16 compact parity tests never cover an unknown-type group (grep for 'unknown' in tests/cli_parity/compact.rs: no hits), so nothing pins either behaviour.

Fix direction: the row lookup should NOT gate silently. Mirror the reference: when a candidate group's type has no registry row, fail with the reference text `Unknown record type: <type>` (exact prefix of mergeRecords' message - probe the reference for the full rendered shape first, including the Error: prefix the CLI adds). The lookup lives in the command (discovery is CLI-shaped per ADR-0005), so this is a command-side fix; the lib law is not involved. A battery test with a twin store + --allow-unknown-types + an unregistered type group belongs in tests/cli_parity/compact.rs (reference-gated) plus an ungated port-side test for the error bytes.

Unassigned by default.

SECOND SURFACE (found by the sprint-45 spec review, same family): the --apply/hook STAMP side. The port's mulch::compact::stamp_id (and the command copy before it) tolerates an unregistered type with a 'content' id-key fallback, while the reference generateRecordId (utils/expertise.ts:113-120) THROWS `Unknown record type: ${record.type}` (registry.get returns undefined). The flag-built --apply types cannot reach it (the command's `other =>` arm rejects unknown types first, commands/compact.rs ~630), but a HOOK-provided replacement (adopt_replacement, ~:814) whose type is unregistered gets stamped mx-<hash> and proceeds where the reference path dies. Fix question to settle when worked: pre-validate the type at the adoption gate (command-side, keeps the lib verdict shape) vs give stamp_id a typed refusal (lib-side; interacts with the mulch-9e28 id unification - read both). The stamp doc in crates/mulch/src/compact.rs now names this deviation explicitly.

The error therefore lives inside find_candidates: both callers propagate `Unknown record type: <type>` as a clean Error line, exit 1, EMPTY stdout, and NO partial write (the first placement had compacted+archived earlier domains before a later one errored - multi-domain test pins alpha untouched). SPRINT-10 SPEC-REVIEW EVIDENCE (2026-10-04, ml 0.10.7) — the unmodelled-subschema family is WIDER than the id pattern: verdict()/full_verdict model only `required`.
